draft.title: Somatic and germline mutations
card: A mutation is a change in the DNA of a cell. Where it happens decides whether it can be passed to offspring.
a mutation in a body cell, such as a skin or liver cell. It stays in that cell and the cells that come from it by mitosis. It is not passed to offspring.
a mutation in a cell that makes gametes (sex cells), such as sperm or egg cells. If that gamete forms a zygote, every cell of the offspring can carry the mutation.
A somatic mutation can still affect the person who has it. A germline mutation may have no effect on the parent, but it can affect the next generation.
draft.remember: Somatic mutations stay in the body. Germline mutations can be inherited.

a.q: Which mutation could be inherited by a child?
opts: A mutation in a sperm-producing cell in the testes
A mutation in a skin cell damaged by sunburn
A mutation in a liver cell of an adult
A mutation in a white blood cell of a mother
a.why: Only a mutation in a cell that makes gametes can be passed on, because the gamete forms the offspring's first cell. Skin, liver and white blood cells are body cells, so their mutations are not inherited.
a.clue: Which cell goes on to make a gamete?

b.q: Leila, a farmer in Dubbo, has a mutation in some skin cells that causes a mole to grow. Her daughter does not have the mutation. What best explains this?
opts: The mutation was somatic, so it was not in her gametes
The mutation was germline, so it was lost in her gametes
The mutation harmed Leila, so it could not be inherited
The mutation happened in the skin, so it was repaired
b.why: A mutation in skin cells is somatic. It stays in those cells and their descendants, so it is not in Leila's gametes. Harm to the parent is not the test: a germline mutation may not affect the parent at all and can still be inherited.
b.clue: Ask which type of cell carried the mutation.

a.best: A mutation in a sperm-producing cell in the testes

b.best: The mutation was somatic, so it was not in her gametes

problems.detail: "a mutation in a cell that makes gametes (sex cells), such as sperm or egg cells" can be read as saying sperm and egg cells make gametes. Sperm and eggs are the gametes themselves. Reword, for example: "a mutation in a gamete (sperm or egg) or in a cell that makes gametes".

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. One card line is ambiguous: it can read as if sperm and egg cells make gametes, when they are the gametes.
